netdiag_mcp.hint_tcp_timeout: Connection timed out (packets dropped or no route). Escalate to the Firewall / Network team with the timestamp and target IP:{port} to check drop logs and routing.
netdiag_mcp.hint_tcp_refused: Connection refused (RST received; host reachable but port not listening). Escalate to the OS / IIS Administrator to check service status and port bindings (or check local nginx if on self-managed RHEL).
netdiag_mcp.hint_tls: TLS/SSL handshake or certificate verification failed (HTTP stage aborted per policy). Share the certificate chain, expiry, SAN, and SHA-256 fingerprint with the Certificate / IIS / OS team (or inspect nginx ssl_certificate if on RHEL).
netdiag_mcp.hint_http: TCP and TLS succeeded; failure occurred at HTTP/edge layer. Share status code, redirect chain, edge trace headers (e.g. CF-Ray / X-Request-Id), and timestamp with the CDN/WAF or Application/IIS/Nginx team.
netdiag_mcp.hint_ok: All stages completed cleanly. If slowness persists, compare TTFB vs total time: high TTFB points to App/DB/IIS Worker, while high TCP RTT or intermittent failures warrant escalating multi-sample metrics to Network.
netdiag_mcp.hint_proxy: Connected via corporate proxy ({proxy}); direct DNS/TCP stages were skipped. Include proxy details if issues only occur behind the proxy.
netdiag_mcp.truncate_hint: Reduce max_stage or samples and retry.
